explanation: This is the one link in the series for which the article gives a mechanism and not only an order. Trincomalee “was the fourth in a series of battles fought between the two fleets off the coast of the Indian subcontinent”, and the article says what put Suffren there: “Suffren and Hughes then met a third time off Negapatam, again with inconclusive results, after which Suffren anchored off Cuddalore to make repairs”, and then — “Due to the exposed nature of the anchorage at Cuddalore, and the impending arrival of additional British fleets, Suffren decided to attempt the capture of Trincomalee to gain a safe harbour for his fleet where he might effect more substantial repairs.” An indecisive battle that left him repairing in an exposed roadstead is why he went for the harbour; `precondition-of` rather than `caused`, because the decision was Suffren's and the article gives him two reasons of which Negapatam is one. Probable: Wikipedia alone.
